Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
322 PM EDT Sat Oct 17 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Frost/freeze coverage is trending lower tonight, especially 
east of the Blue Ridge. Extended Small Craft Advisories into 
Sunday. Lowered minimum temperatures and added mention of frost 
Sunday night west of I-95.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Below normal temperatures with frost and freeze concerns
  continue through Monday morning.

- 2) A Nor'easter lurks nearby for the new workweek bringing the
  potential for a few showers and breezy conditions, especially
  along and east of I-95.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Below normal temperatures with frost and freeze
concerns continue through Monday morning.

The mid level trough axis is moving across the area this 
afternoon. Anafrontal rain is now exiting southern Maryland. 
Drier air in the wake of the upper jet streak is seen in water 
vapor imagery, with the clearing line reaching the I-95 
corridor. Temperatures are holding in the 50s this afternoon, 
although more sunshine and deep mixing have allowed them to warm
a few degrees higher than the previous forecast. Northerly 
winds gusting 20-35 mph continue through the afternoon before 
decreasing tonight.

The trends has continued tonight to keep the center of the
surface high over the upper Ohio Valley. There will be a sharper
pressure gradient on its southeastern flank due to the
developing Nor'easter off the North Carolina coast. While it was
already expected to some extent, winds remaining at least 5 mph
will likely limit how much temperatures can fall east of the 
Blue Ridge. Tonight's cold air will be driven more by advection,
although more widespread decoupling may occur west of the Blue 
Ridge closer to the surface high. The elevated winds may 
maintain notable temperature/dew point spreads (the latter of 
which will be in the upper 20s) to prevent widespread frost 
formation, especially east of the Blue Ridge. The Frost Advisory
remains in effect though, since many of these areas in the 
piedmont are prone to localized decoupling. While NBM 
probabilities of freezing temperatures have decreased from 
yesterday, especially east of the Blue Ridge, reliable guidance 
does still show pockets of freezing temperatures in the Freeze 
Warning area. The highest confidence in widespread subfreezing 
temperatures is in the Allegheny and Potomac Highlands, perhaps 
over to the central Shenandoah Valley. So in the end, no changes
to those headlines at this time.

The high settles more directly over the area Sunday into Sunday
night, leading to lighter winds and continued dry conditions.
The pressure gradient will increase to the southeast though, so
winds may be a bit more elevated over southern Maryland. Highs
will remain below normal in the mid 50s to near 60. The 
position of the high might actually lead to colder conditions in
some areas Sunday night into Monday morning, especially between
I-81 and US-15. Dew points in the upper 20s and lower 30s along
with calm winds make a case for more potential for frost and 
freeze conditions west of I-95. Headline decisions will need to
wait until it is determined where the growing season will
continue after tonight.

A gradual warming trend likely starts thereafter, although
temperatures will remain below normal through Monday night. 
While there is some uncertainty with the Nor'easter off the 
Carolina coast, most guidance keeps it far enough to the 
southeast for dry conditions to continue through Monday night.

KEY MESSAGE 2...A Nor'easter lurks nearby for the new workweek
bringing the potential for a few showers and breezy conditions,
especially along and east of I-95.

Uncertainty remains regarding a potential nor'easter developing in 
the vicinity of the NC/VA coast during the early and middle part of 
next week. The track of this system will dictate any rain chances, 
breezy conditions, and coastal flooding risks across the region. 
Current 12z guidance remains all over the place when it comes to the 
placement of the low and timing as it meanders along the coast. Each 
of the models form a coastal low on what was the residual upper 
level trough and front from earlier in the weekend. Guidance points 
to a low either along the coast of NC or 25-50 miles offshore Monday 
before drifting it north toward the Delmarva and NJ coast midweek. 
Some of the guidance even retrogrades the low back into southern NJ 
and the Delmarva during the back half of the workweek period. 
Meanwhile, 1035-1037 mb high pressure will remain wedged along 
and west of the mountains Monday into Tuesday before retreating 
east midweek. A secondary area of 1028-1030 mb Canadian high 
pressure will follow Wednesday and Thursday as it slides east 
from Ontario into New England before wedging south late week. 
It's not until next week when a front crosses the region. 

Synoptically, we sit in an omega block type setup under 
predominantly zonal flow. The coastal low offshore combined with the 
wedging high in the east, ridging in the center part of the country, 
and troughiness in the west. With that said, expect the nor'easter 
to have little movement along the coast throughout the week. As the 
low fills and potentially occludes Tuesday through Friday, expect 
spokes of shortwave energy to pivot it along it. These spokes of 
energy will drive any shower threat, especially in locations along 
and east of I-95. The highest probabilities for rain (at least 
20 percent) remain across southern MD, the northern neck of VA, 
and perhaps northeast MD during the Monday through Friday 
timeframe. Areas further west will likely remain dry with a few 
passing clouds. Downsloping west of the Blue Ridge will keep dry
conditions in place throughout the week. Outside the shower 
chances will be the concern for wind, marine issues, and coastal
flooding. Right now, winds look to average between 15 to 25 mph
during the Monday afternoon through Wednesday afternoon 
timeframe. Highest gusts of 25 to perhaps 35 mph will be down 
across southern MD and along the western shore of the Bay where 
the gradient will be tighter compared to locations west. As for 
marine and coastal flooding concerns see the corresponding 
discussions below. 

Highs temperatures will top out in the mid to upper 60s (50s 
mountains) each day with overnight lows in the upper 30s and mid 
40s. Overnight lows warm into the 50s late week. 

&&

.AVIATION /18Z SATURDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
With clouds clearing to the east, the main concern for the TAFs
is the wind. Northerly gusts of 20-30 kt will subside with
sunset, although some 15-20 kt gusts may linger the first half
of the night. High pressure will build closer by Sunday into
Monday, but a nor'easter will lurk off the Carolina coast. Any 
north or northeasterly gusts to 20 kt will be limited to the 
daytime hours. Dry conditions will continue with few or no 
clouds.

Tuesday through Saturday...Primarily VFR conditions are expected 
amongst the terminals with periods of sub-VFR mainly east of BWI, 
DCA, and MTN. A few showers are possible on the east side of the ZDC 
airspace with the nor'easter lurking offshore. Winds will generally 
be out of the northeast at 10 to 20 kts with gusts up to 30 kts, 
especially near the waters. 

&&

.MARINE...
Gusty northerly winds continue this afternoon in the wake of a 
strong cold front. Marginal gale gusts continue south of the Bay
Bridge. The Gale Warning continues until 6 AM Sunday, but recent
trends suggest winds may drop below criteria before that point,
perhaps as early as this evening. Elsewhere, Small Craft
Advisories continue. The upper Potomac is expected to drop below
criteria late this evening, but the remainder of the waters
likely won't see wholesale decreases in winds until sometime
Sunday morning. Locations south of the Bay Bridge and the lower
Potomac will likely keep advisory conditions most of Sunday.
Advisories were issued or extended accordingly. Advisories will
likely need to be extended into Sunday night for portions of the
waters, although the coverage will depend on the position and
strength of a Nor'easter off the North Carolina coast.

Monday through Thursday...A developing nor'easter off the Mid-
Atlantic coast will deliver a prolonged period of SCA conditions
and potential gales (mainly over the wider waters of the mid 
bay). Confidence is currently low for gales based upon the track
of the system with projected winds out of the northeast at 
10-20 kts with gusts up to 30 kts at times. 

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
After approaching near-blowout conditions in the northern bay
this afternoon, a snapback likely begins tonight as northerly
winds begin to slacken. A developing nor'easter off the Mid- 
Atlantic coast will lead to tidal anomalies rising more into the
upcoming week. Sensitive locations (i.e Annapolis) will have a 
chance to reach minor flooding thresholds during the high tide 
cycle Sunday night and again during the middle of next week. 
Considerable uncertainty remains on how exactly this Nor'easter 
will track and subsequently affect the tide levels.

&&

.LWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
DC...None.
MD...Small Craft Advisory until 11 AM EDT Sunday for MDZ008.
     Freeze Warning from 1 AM to 9 AM EDT Sunday for MDZ003>006-501-
     502-507-509-510.
     Frost Advisory from 1 AM to 9 AM EDT Sunday for MDZ503-505.
VA...Freeze Warning from 1 AM to 9 AM EDT Sunday for VAZ025>031-
     503>505-507-508.
     Frost Advisory from 1 AM to 9 AM EDT Sunday for VAZ036>040-050-
     051-501-502-506-526.
WV...Freeze Warning from 1 AM to 9 AM EDT Sunday for WVZ050>053-055-
     501>506.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory until 11 AM EDT Sunday for ANZ530-531-538-
     539.
     Gale Warning until 6 AM EDT Sunday for ANZ532>534-537-543.
     Small Craft Advisory from 6 AM to 6 PM EDT Sunday for 
     ANZ532>534-537-543.
     Small Craft Advisory until 11 PM EDT this evening for ANZ535.
     Small Craft Advisory until 6 AM EDT Sunday for ANZ536.
     Small Craft Advisory until 6 PM EDT Sunday for ANZ540>542.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...ADS/EST
AVIATION...ADS/EST
